quote: the effect of Default was due to the difference between the Participate and Not Participate groups (t ¼ 4.59, p < .001)
reason: Reconciling the prior response, rejecting df = 2 is not based on its absence from the text and the full formatted statistic expression 't = 4.59' should be preserved rather than bare '4.59'. In Experiment 2's 2 (Frame) x 3 (Default) binary logistic regression on N = 235 respondents (overall model chi^2(5) = 28.2, p < .001), the printed t = 4.59 for the pairwise Participate vs. Not Participate contrast is a 1-df asymptotic coefficient-to-SE (Wald) ratio with no finite degrees of freedom, and a finite t(2) distribution (misappropriated from the 3-level Default factor's k - 1 = 2 omnibus df) is mathematically contradicted by the reported p < .001 bound because t(2) = 4.59 yields p = .044 two-tailed (.022 one-tailed) whereas the asymptotic normal reference distribution yields p = 4.4e-6 < .001.
